name: Sintra
seoTitle: Sintra on a Cruise Call: Which Sites to Pick and How
tagline: Sintra rewards a long port call if you pick one or two sites, book ahead and keep a firm train home.

description.short: The hill town 30 km west of Lisbon that holds Pena, Regaleira, the Moorish Castle, the National Palace and Monserrate. From the cruise terminal it is 75 to 90 minutes each way, so the real decision is which one or two sites to see.
description.full:
Sintra's hills hold five major sights, and a cruise passenger can see one or two of them properly. This page is about choosing, not about seeing everything.

Getting there takes 75 to 90 minutes each way from the Jardim do Tabaco terminal: a 10-minute walk to Santa Apolónia, the metro Blue Line to Restauradores, a two-minute walk to Rossio station, then the CP train to Sintra (about 40 minutes). With about three hours of travel and a safety margin, Sintra makes sense only on calls of eight to nine hours or more, with tickets bought before you sail.

The sights fall into three groups, and the groups decide your day. In the lower town, on foot from the station, are the National Palace of Sintra (10 to 15 minutes' walk) and Quinta da Regaleira (20 to 25 minutes). No bus is needed, which removes the biggest source of delay. On the hilltop, reached by Scotturb bus 434, are Pena and the Moorish Castle; their entrances are a short walk apart on the same road, but the bus queue at the station can add 30 to 60 minutes in summer. West of town, on bus 435 or Carris Metropolitana 1253, is Monserrate, a quieter garden estate on the road to Colares.

On a call of about nine hours, pick one site and add a walk through the town centre. On ten hours or more, pick one pair that shares a route: Pena with the Moorish Castle, the National Palace with Regaleira, or Regaleira with Monserrate, which are both on bus 435. Avoid mixing the hilltop with Monserrate: there is no direct bus between them, so you have to come back down to town and change.

Scotturb's 24-hour ticket covers lines 434 and 435 (10.96 euros online). The Lisboa Card is not valid on these buses, and the combined CP Train&Bus ticket is currently suspended. Whatever you choose, aim to be back at Rossio at least 90 minutes before all-aboard.
description.history: People have lived on the Sintra hills since the Neolithic. Under Islamic rule the Moorish Castle guarded the land and sea approaches to Lisbon, and in 1147 Sintra passed to Afonso Henriques, the first king of Portugal. For the next seven centuries the palace in the town centre was a royal residence, used for hunting, summer retreats and refuge from plague in Lisbon. The 19th century brought the Romantic estates: Ferdinand II bought the ruined monastery of Pena in 1838 and restored the castle walls, and the British collector Francis Cook remade Monserrate from 1863. Between about 1904 and 1910 Carvalho Monteiro and Luigi Manini added Quinta da Regaleira. In 1995 UNESCO listed the whole area as the Cultural Landscape of Sintra.
description.significance: UNESCO listed Sintra in 1995 as a cultural landscape, describing it as the first centre of European Romantic architecture, where 19th-century owners shaped forest, gardens and buildings into one designed whole. In practical terms, the sights are only a few kilometres apart but on very different levels, from the town centre at the foot of the hills to Pena near the summit. That geography, more than distance, limits how much a cruise passenger can see.

directions.general: Located in the Serra de Sintra mountains, 28km northwest of Lisbon
directions.fromCruisePort: Walk about 10 minutes to Santa Apolónia and take the metro Blue Line to Restauradores; Rossio station is a two-minute walk. Trains from Rossio reach Sintra in about 40 minutes. The National Palace and Quinta da Regaleira are walkable from Sintra station; Pena and the Moorish Castle are on Scotturb bus 434, and Monserrate on bus 435 or Carris Metropolitana 1253. Allow 75 to 90 minutes door to door each way.
directions.publicTransport: CP train from Lisbon Rossio to Sintra (about 40 minutes), paid with a Navegante ocasional card (0.50 euros, reusable). In Sintra, Scotturb bus 434 serves the Moorish Castle and Pena, bus 435 serves Quinta da Regaleira and Monserrate; a 24-hour ticket for both lines costs 10.96 euros online. The Lisboa Card is not valid on 434 or 435.
directions.parking: Limited parking in Sintra center. Pena Palace and major palaces have paid parking lots (often full). Park & Ride from train station recommended.

openingTimes.currentStatus: Town always open. Parques de Sintra monuments and Quinta da Regaleira open daily except 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January

admissionPrices.notes: The town itself is free. 2026 adult prices (18-64): Pena Essential Visit 20 euros or Park only 12 euros; Quinta da Regaleira 20 euros; National Palace of Sintra 13 euros; Moorish Castle 12 euros; Monserrate 12 euros. Youths and seniors pay less at every site. Scotturb 24-hour ticket for buses 434 and 435: 10.96 euros online. The CP Train&Bus combined ticket is currently suspended.

visitingInformation.averageVisitDuration: About 2 hours per site, plus about 3 hours of travel from the port
visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Arrive by about 10:00, before the day-trip coaches. Weekdays outside July and August are quieter. Clear days matter for Pena and the Moorish Castle.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Choose one or two sites that share a route and buy tickets online before you sail. Pena needs a timed slot; the other Parques de Sintra monuments sell date tickets. Wear shoes with grip and carry a light layer: the hills are often cooler and mistier than Lisbon.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 5 hours door to door for one site and 6.5-7 hours for two; realistic only on calls of 8-9 hours or more
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Metro, a 40-minute train and then steep cobbled streets or a winding bus ride. The National Palace is the most manageable sight; Pena, the Moorish Castle and Regaleira involve steep paths and many steps.
combinableWith: Palácio da Pena + Castelo dos Mouros (bus 434)
National Palace of Sintra + Quinta da Regaleira (on foot)
Quinta da Regaleira + Palácio de Monserrate (bus 435)
tips: Pick your site before you sail and buy the ticket online: Pena needs a timed slot, the other Parques de Sintra monuments sell date tickets that can be rescheduled online until 18:00 the day before.
The National Palace and Quinta da Regaleira are walkable from Sintra station, so a lower-town day avoids the bus 434 queue entirely.

Bus 434 loops from the station through the town centre up to the Moorish Castle and Pena, then back; bus 435 runs to Regaleira, Seteais and Monserrate. There is no direct bus between Pena and Monserrate.
Scotturb's 24-hour ticket for 434 and 435 costs 10.96 euros online and can also be bought on board; the Lisboa Card is not valid on these lines.
The CP Train&Bus combined ticket is currently suspended: buy the train fare at Rossio on a Navegante ocasional card (0.50 euros) and the bus ticket separately.
Parques de Sintra sites close on 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January, and can close at short notice for very high fire risk or storms; check the official notices page on the morning of your visit.
For a quick lunch, eat in the town centre rather than at the hilltop cafés; Piriquita is known for travesseiros.
Be back at Rossio at least 90 minutes before all-aboard; the Sintra line can be delayed and the return has a deadline.

highlights: National Palace of Sintra, in the town centre, 10-15 minutes' walk from the station
Quinta da Regaleira, with the Initiation Well and tunnels, at the edge of the historic centre
Palácio da Pena and its park near the summit, on bus 434
Moorish Castle walls, a short walk from the Pena entrance on the same bus route
Monserrate, a quieter botanical park west of town on bus 435
Historic centre lanes and pastry shops selling travesseiros and queijadas
Santa Maria trail, a marked footpath from the centre up to the Moorish Castle
facilities: Train station with connections to Lisbon

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Challenging for visitors with mobility issues. Steep hills throughout town and palace grounds. Pena Palace has 300+ steps to reach from parking; shuttle available but limited capacity. Quinta da Regaleira has many stairs including spiral staircase in Initiation Well. Moorish Castle requires significant stair climbing. National Palace more accessible but still has stairs. Bus 434 is accessible. Some restaurants in town center accessible. Recommend advance planning for limited mobility visitors.
